input.name: A new app in ten minutes (the golden path)
input.description: From `paperos create` to a deployed, themed, data-backed app with a repo, in ten minutes, by 2026-10-01.
input.content:
**Outcome.** A founder (or an agent acting for one) runs `paperos create`, answers the app interview, and ten minutes later has a running app: a monorepo scaffolded from the template, a `page.spec.yaml`-driven set of pages generated by the Spec Builder, tokens and components from the Design System, Postgres with Drizzle and local-first sync from the Data Layer, a Forgejo repository mirrored to GitHub, and a deploy on the VPS. PAP-29 is the acceptance test: the blank-screen-to-running-app drill with timed checkpoints C1-C5.

**Why it matters.** This is the answer to PAP-5 and the reason the platform exists. Every other initiative (agents, product surfaces, business modules) plugs into the shell this path produces; if the golden path is slow or brittle, nothing built on top of it is worth shipping. It is also the demo Justin can run himself without reading a spec.

**How we know it is done.** PAP-29 completes in under ten minutes on staging twice in a row; RC2 (09-28) and RC3 (10-01) both pass the drill; the six projects here have every non-deferred issue Done or Canceled with a reason; `imagine-os/paperos-template` has a tagged `v0.1.0`.

**Read first:** [New App in Ten Minutes: the golden path](https://linear.app/paperos/document/new-app-in-ten-minutes-the-golden-path-0f49429f566e), [PaperOS Core Platform Blueprint](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-core-platform-blueprint-0c2115fe48f1), [PaperOS Module System](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-module-system-8007373cc6bb), [PaperOS Interface & Data Contracts](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-interface-and-data-contracts-d40e6a4d227c). Specs: `specs/app-shell`, `specs/spec-builder`, `specs/design-system`, `specs/forge`, `specs/data-layer`, `specs/libraries` in `imagine-os/linear-builder`.

input.name: The agent org runs the build
input.description: Nine lead characters and their sub-agents claim from Ready for Claude, build in worktrees, pass Sentinel's gates and ship without a human in the loop except Needs Justin.
input.content:
**Outcome.** Linear team PAP is the system of record and the orchestrator (PAP-96) is the only thing that promotes and claims issues. Each session runs as a named character from the roster with its own tool allowlist, budget and memory, works in a worktree on `feat/PAP-n-<slug>`, and hands its PR to the Quality Pipeline (Gates 1-4). Every module obeys the Module System: a manifest, a versioned `@paperos/contract-<module>` package, a conformance suite and a kernel registry, so a module can be swapped by flag and rewritten without touching its neighbours.

**Why it matters.** Justin is the only human. The plan is 485 canonical issues on 18 projects in two weeks at up to 20 parallel sessions; that only works if claiming, reviewing, budgeting and escalation are mechanical. The agent org is also a product: the same characters, skills and evals ship inside PaperOS for its customers (Agent Characters & Orgs).

**How we know it is done.** The orchestrator claims and ships issues end to end from 09-20 pm (Execution Schedule); Gate 2 runs on every PR from 09-21; the eval harness (PAP-110) has golden tasks for every lead character; the shell-swap drill (PAP-446) passes; the daily burn report (PAP-98) posts at 09:00Z; `Needs Justin` never holds more than five open cards.

**Read first:** [PaperOS Agent Roster](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-agent-roster-org-chart-and-character-index-fc7ea7f41ff3), [PaperOS Execution Schedule](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-execution-schedule-1fa3d38d6795), [PaperOS Module System](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-module-system-8007373cc6bb), [PaperOS Security & Threat Model](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-security-and-threat-model-51fd5fd8929c) (section 4, the agent deny list). Specs: `specs/pm-linear`, `specs/agents`, `specs/quality`, `specs/module-system`.

input.name: Product surfaces for every audience
input.description: Tables and views, comments and docs, realtime multiplayer, every input device, and one identity model with roles and audiences from customer to agent.
input.content:
**Outcome.** A generated PaperOS app is usable by customers, staff, partners, admins and agents on phone, tablet, desktop, kiosk and TV. The Table & Views Engine is a superset of Airtable, Notion and ClickUp views on top of the shared filter grammar; comments anchor anywhere and can become Linear issues; documents, changelogs and the prompt log live in-app; Yjs-backed realtime keeps records and canvases in sync with offline support; keyboard, touch, pen, gamepad and voice all drive the same input abstraction; and the audience model plus RLS-backed permissions decide who sees what, including agent principals.

**Why it matters.** These are the surfaces every business module renders through and the features customers compare against incumbents. They are also where accessibility (WCAG conformance report, PAP-160) and multi-tenant safety (PAP-227-229) are proven or lost.

**How we know it is done.** RC1 (09-24) has RLS-backed permissions and the Yjs server; RC2 (09-28) has the grid and compiler (PAP-163, 165), comments (PAP-131) and record sync (PAP-143); the parity checklist (PAP-162) is met for the v0.1 view types; the accessibility certification milestone (Multi-Input, 09-30) has evidence attached; every deferred issue in these projects is moved to the v0.2 milestone at NJ-19.

**Read first:** [PaperOS Interface & Data Contracts](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-interface-and-data-contracts-d40e6a4d227c) (FilterTree, Principal, event envelope), [Round 2 pending issues: tables (24)](https://linear.app/paperos/document/round-2-pending-issues-tables-24-86486d9b99cc), [PaperOS Module System](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-module-system-8007373cc6bb), [PaperOS Security & Threat Model](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-security-and-threat-model-51fd5fd8929c). Specs: `specs/tables`, `specs/collab`, `specs/realtime`, `specs/input`, `specs/identity`.

input.name: Business-ready for any business
input.description: Payments, ledger, invoicing and payroll; CRM, campaigns and outreach; importers from Airtable, Notion, ClickUp, HubSpot and QuickBooks so a real business can move in.
input.content:
**Outcome.** A PaperOS app can run a small business on day one: Stripe billing with products, subscriptions and a customer portal; a double-entry ledger, invoices and reports; a payroll adapter behind a provider port (Check by default, NJ-12); a CRM core with campaigns, social scheduling and a support inbox; and an import framework with CSV and Airtable, Notion and ClickUp importers plus business migrations from Stripe and QuickBooks/Xero. The content agent (PAP-192) and migration agent (PAP-208) are the first customer-facing characters.

**Why it matters.** The golden path proves the platform; these three projects prove it can carry revenue and replace the tools a business already pays for. They are P2 in the schedule and are the first to be cut by the stop-loss rules, so they must land against mocks early and swap in real credentials the moment Justin provides them.

**How we know it is done.** RC2 (09-28) has the ledger and invoices (PAP-179, 180) and imports (PAP-199); Stripe test mode works from RC1 (PAP-177); the demo tenant is billed, invoiced and imported from an Airtable base end to end; NJ-10, NJ-12, NJ-13 and NJ-16 are answered or defaulted; deferred growth and migration issues move to v0.2 at NJ-19. Health is `atRisk` until those credential asks resolve.

**Read first:** [PaperOS Core Platform Blueprint](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-core-platform-blueprint-0c2115fe48f1), [PaperOS Interface & Data Contracts](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-interface-and-data-contracts-d40e6a4d227c) (Money, idempotency), [PaperOS Security & Threat Model](https://linear.app/paperos/document/paperos-security-and-threat-model-51fd5fd8929c) (PCI SAQ-A posture), [Round 2 pending issues: business-core (11)](https://linear.app/paperos/document/round-2-pending-issues-business-core-11-7c8c2526b3c9), [Round 2 pending issues: growth (13)](https://linear.app/paperos/document/round-2-pending-issues-growth-13-3fd4406e8012), [Round 2 pending issues: migration (20)](https://linear.app/paperos/document/round-2-pending-issues-migration-20-6cb063cc1be6). Specs: `specs/business-core`, `specs/growth`, `specs/migration`.

Goal: one paragraph on what this module gives the platform and for whom. Non-goal: what it leaves to a neighbour.

## Contract

**Provides**

* `@paperos/contract-<module>`: types, Zod schemas, event topics, oRPC route signatures, UI slot definitions, repository ports, conformance suite and golden fixtures (never runtime code).
* Tables, routes and components owned by this module (list them by issue).

**Consumes**

* Other modules' contract packages only, resolved through the `@paperos/kernel` registry (PAP-434), event bus, gateway (PAP-437), UI slots (PAP-438) and config port (PAP-444).

**Module trio** (one issue each; see the PaperOS Module System document)

1. Publish `@paperos/contract-<module>` v0.1
2. Conformance test suite for <module>
3. Wire <module> behind the module registry with an adapter and feature flag

## Milestones

1. <Milestone 1: contract published and kernel wiring> (date)
2. <Milestone 2: core surfaces work end to end> (date)
3. <Milestone 3: conformance green, swap drill passes> (date)

## Reading

Blueprint, Interface & Data Contracts, PaperOS Module System, this project's specs under `specs/<module>/`.
